text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: elevated invocation timeouts and 502/504 rates detected for /v1/generate across canary cluster in us-west-2. p95 -> 1.2s (baseline 350ms), p99 -> 3.8s (baseline 600ms). Error rate 5xx spike to 6.4% over last 3m. Triggered by deploy 2026-03-15T10:32Z to canary group. Auto-fallback not yet engaged.

Nina (oncall): saw the page, oncall here. Confirming — is this only canary or are we seeing routed host traffic? 

Alex J: only canary lanes so far. Telemetry shows connection timeouts at the gateway layer -> increased upstream wait. Early suspicion: new kernel selection path in runtime that changed spin/poll behavior.

Sasha P: adding logs from the canary pods: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:33:10Z] request_id=tx-9a1e upstream_wait=1.1s kv_cache_miss=true model=redwood-v2-onnx
[2026-03-15T10:33:11Z] request_id=tx-9a1f error=upstream_timeout code=504
```
Noting a sudden jump in kv_cache_miss ratio after deploy.

Marta L: can we check the runtime config that landed? I pushed a change to kernel selection heuristics and a small batching tweak in the same PR. PR#4821.

Ryan C: confirming PR#4821. It toggles the `prefer_attention_accel` flag for certain sequence lengths. Might change thread affinity and polling. I can revert that flag remotely if needed.

Nina (oncall): we need immediate mitigation. Options: 1) roll the canary back to previous revision, 2) flip off the new kernel flag via runtime feature flag, 3) autoscale canary to add headroom. Which is fastest?

Alex J: fastest is rollback. Flipping the flag requires a config push across many nodes; rollout might still take a few minutes. Autoscaling won't help if it's a perf regression on each pod. +1 rollback.

Sasha P: agreed. Initiating rollback now. Command: 
```
# rollback canary deployment to stable revision
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/redwood-runtime-canary --to-revision=42
```
I'll watch for pod readiness and tail the logs.

incidents-bot: ACTION: rollback started by Sasha P at 2026-03-15T10:34:05Z. Notifying pager duty.

Nina (oncall): copying status to #product-ops and accounts. Product Ops, please prepare a brief for affected customers. Estimate impact window: ~10:32Z - until rollback finishes.

Product Ops: ack. We'll draft an internal blameless summary and customer-facing note (chart + timeline). Which customers hit error spike?

Alex J: looking at tenant telemetry: high-volume API keys A-233, B-77, C-19 saw >5% error spike. We'll produce per-tenant qps/error tables in 5m.

Sasha P: pods are terminating and new replicas of revision=42 are coming up. Readiness probes passing on 3/3 in the first batch.

incidents-bot: MONITOR: p95 dropped back to 420ms and p99 to 610ms within 90s of rollback. 5xx rate down to 0.8% over last 2m.

Nina (oncall): good. Holding incident open for 30m to watch for recurrence. Postmortem owner? Suggest Alex J + Sasha P.

Marta L: I'll help with root cause once we collect kernel selection traces. Initial hypothesis: changed polling affinity caused longer upstream waits and higher KV cache churn. We'll run A/B repros against the problematic seq distribution.

Ryan C: I'll prepare a canary test matrix and add a blocking safelist for kernel changes until we have perf regressions tests.

Product Ops: drafting customer note: short incident, canary-only deploy, rollback completed, impact window ~2.5m. Will propose outreach to top affected tenants.

Nina (oncall): assigning severity SEV3 (customer-facing but limited to canary traffic). Next: postmortem in #incidents-docs, timeline + telemetry + remediation actions. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
